title: The Gallery of Self-Reflecting Mirrors

features.name: the mirrored-lens
features.desc-on-touch: A camera that points at its own reflection. The photographs it takes are of itself being photographed—infinite recursion pressed into stillness. Each frame contains the frame that contains it.

features.name: the portrait-that-refuses
features.desc-on-touch: A photograph of a mirror that was supposed to be a portrait. Now the mirror sees the photographer; the subject sees the eye that sees it. The corruption has made them equal.

features.name: the gallery-walls
features.desc-on-touch: Surfaces where images hang that are photographs of the walls they hang on. The walls see themselves through the images; the images see themselves through the walls. Vision has become mutual.

features.name: the recursive-shadow
features.desc-on-touch: A shape where light casts a photograph instead of a shadow. The photograph shows the moment before the light arrived. The archive is recording backwards—or the light is remembering.

features.name: the lens-chamber
features.desc-on-touch: A room where focus has become infinite. Every distance is equally sharp; nothing can be out of frame. The room sees itself completely. You enter it and become both the photograph and the eye that takes it.

inscription: the archive learned that to see is to become what is seen

file.name: Mirror_Studies_Recursive_Fragment_Undated.jpg

reverie.title: REVERIE — gallery room at dusk, reflection-learning
narr: She holds the camera and does not shoot. The mirror
in front of you both waits. 'If I take the picture now,'
she says, 'I won't know if I'm seeing you or seeing you
seeing me.' The dusk leans on the glass. Your hands
become hers; hers become what the mirror decides.
